editorial:
The Vampire Bat is a Majestic Pictures horror film directed by Frank R. Strayer and released on January 10, 1933. Lionel Atwill plays Dr. Otto von Niemann, with Fay Wray, Melvyn Douglas and Dwight Frye in the cast. Its village-murder plot and its cast make it a ready source for horror compilations, clip reels and film-history work.

The print is the free part. A 1933 film needed a renewal around 1961 to keep its copyright. A text check of the 1960, 1961 and 1962 Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volumes found no renewal for this title or for Majestic Pictures. The trap is the layers around the print. I did not clear the music or the story credit (Edward T. Lowe Jr.), and I found no restoration to rule out added material. Trademark is also unchecked. Use a copy whose provenance you can document, and check any modern transfer for new titles or a new score.
faq: Is The Vampire Bat's print free to use in the US?

The print appears to be free. No renewal for the 1933 film turned up in the 1960, 1961 or 1962 Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volumes. The score, story and trademark layers were not cleared, so verify them for any commercial reuse.
Can I use the Internet Archive copy?

The Internet Archive copy is described as transferred from an original film print, so it is a reasonable source. Avoid copies with added music, titles or colorization, because those additions can carry their own rights.
